what_happened: The person running Athena deleted by hand the 9.8 GB writer build folder of job 20261031-082442-92qg (the focus-and-caps job). The job was held on low disk, not failed. The checks stage's 10 GB free-space check runs before the writer's build is removed. So the job was held because of its own build, even though its checks would come from GitHub and need no local build. No acceptance criterion or check had failed. It was an environment stop. A fix was queued.
cause: Athena has no disk lifecycle that is tied to a build's own state. The free-space guard and the build-freeing step were added as separate changes, and nothing fixes their order or checks that they agree. The guard counts a regenerable build as space the job needs, and it does not ask whether the job still needs that build. The hold only waits, and the held job's own build is what blocks its resume. The fix is again an ordinary queued job that has not been made urgent, although this is at least the seventh hand cleanup in this class in a few days.
prevention: Give Athena one disk lifecycle. Before the low-disk check and before any hold, the writer's regenerable build is removed once the writer has finished and its output is committed or recorded. The guard then measures free space after that removal. Where checks come from GitHub, the guard does not count the local build at all. If the job is still under the limit after reclaiming its own regenerable builds, the hold may apply. A test should run the checks stage with a finished writer build present and free space just under 10 GB. It should assert that the build is removed first and the job is not held.
proposed_request: Fix the order of the disk guard and build removal in the checks stage. Outcome: a job is never held or failed on low disk because of its own finished writer build. Once the writer has finished and its work is recorded, Athena removes that regenerable build before the 10 GB free-space check runs, and the check measures free space after the removal. When checks come from GitHub, the local build is not counted. A job is held only if space is still under the limit after its own regenerable builds are removed. Acceptance: (1) a test with a finished writer build present and free space just under 10 GB, where removing the build brings space over the limit, shows the job proceeds to checks and is not held; (2) a test where space stays under the limit after removal shows the job is held with the free-space message; (3) a test where checks come from GitHub shows the build is removed and not counted; (4) the build is not removed while the writer is still running or before its output is recorded; (5) existing disk-guard and hold tests still pass. Mark this request high priority, since it has caused repeated hand cleanups.
